Wyllie worked with charities and associations related to India. At a reception given by one such association - the National Indian Association - in 1909, Wyllie was shot by Madan Lal Dhingra, an Indian student. A Parsee physician, Dr Cawas Lalcaca, who sought to protect Wyllie, was also killed. Dhingra and his family were known to Wyllie from his time in India, and Dhingra's family had maintained a correspondence with Wyllie. Dhingra had himself ignored letters from Wyllie suggesting a meeting at India House. Some argue that Dhingra's preferred target was either the former Secretary of State Lord Morley or the former Viceroy Lord Curzon, given their greater prestige and connection with the construction of repressive policies against revolutionaries in India; Dhingra was known to have been following both men. Wyllie's presence at events with Indian students, however, made him an easier target.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The woodcutter felled / some trees / with hardly / many effort at all.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The woodcutter felled / some trees / with hardly / many effort at all.
questions.solution:
'Hardly' means 'scarcely' (used to qualify a statement by saying that it is true to an insignificant degree).

This means that the woodcutter did not even have to make any effort at all and he felled some trees, implying that he did not make many efforts. So, the determiner 'many' is incorrectly used here.

It should be replaced with 'any'. Also, the determiner 'many' could not be followed by the singular noun 'effort'.

The correct sentence is: The woodcutter felled some trees with hardly any effort at all.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Among - happening or being included as part of a group of people or things

Through - moving in one side and out of the other side of (an opening, channel, or location).

Along - moving in a constant direction on (a road, path, or any more or less horizontal surface).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'. "Can you give me so many examples of subordinate clauses?", the teacher asked the class.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

"Can you give me so many examples of subordinate clauses?", the teacher asked the class.
questions.solution:
The given sentence implies that the teacher is asking for some examples of subordinate clauses.

The underlined part requires substitution as 'so many' is not the appropriate phrase to ask for some examples as 'so many' implies the intensity ('very' or extremely') which is not implied the sentence.

'So many' could be correct in the following sentence: He gave so many examples of subordinate clauses that it impressed the teacher. Here, the sentence implies intensity.

'Some' and 'few' mean the same. So, 'some' followed by 'few' would create the redundancy error. So, option (d) is negated.

'Some' means 'a few', and 'many' means 'a large number of'. Both these words cannot be used simultaneously. So, option (a) is negated.

'Some more examples' would imply a greater number of examples than previously given. This makes the sentence meaningful.

The correct sentence is: "Can you give me some more examples of subordinate clauses?", the teacher asked the class.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The sunrays burned my face.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The sunrays burned my face.

options.text: My face is burned by the sunrays.
options.html: My face is burned by the sunrays.

options.text: My face was burned by the sunrays.
options.html: My face was burned by the sunrays.

options.text: My face has been burned by the sunrays.
options.html: My face has been burned by the sunrays.

options.text: My face is being burned by the sunrays.
options.html: My face is being burned by the sunrays.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): My face was burned by the sunrays.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. "is he alright now?" I asked my neighbour's wife about her husband, Mr.Gulyani.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

"is he alright now?" I asked my neighbour's wife about her husband, Mr.Gulyani.

options.text: I asked Mrs. Gulyani, my neighbour's wife, if her husband had become alright then.
options.html: I asked Mrs. Gulyani, my neighbour's wife, if her husband had become alright then.

options.text: I asked Mrs. Gulyani, my neighbour's wife, if her husband is alright now.

options.text: I asked Mrs. Gulyani, my neighbour's wife, if her husband was alright then.
options.html: I asked Mrs. Gulyani, my neighbour's wife, if her husband was alright then.

questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in the Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Present Simple tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Past Simple tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'If' will be added in the sentence.

'Is' will be changed to 'was'.

'Now' will be changed to 'then'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): I asked Mrs. Gulyani, my neighbour's wife, if her husband was alright then.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given in jumbled order. Arrange the sentence in the right order to form meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. While India is home to 75 per cent of the tigers in the world, the Global Tiger Day, as it is also known - sees awareness events organised in the country, as well as in neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal. B. Its primary objective is to preserve the natural habitat of the tiger. C. International Tiger Day was initiated in 2010, at the saint Petersburg Tiger Summit. D. This annual event observed on 29 July, aims to create awareness on tiger conservation.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given in jumbled order. Arrange the sentence in the right order to form meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. While India is home to 75 per cent of the tigers in the world, the Global Tiger Day, as it is also known - sees awareness events organised in the country, as well as in neighbouring Bangladesh and Nepal.

B. Its primary objective is to preserve the natural habitat of the tiger.

C. International Tiger Day was initiated in 2010, at the saint Petersburg Tiger Summit.

D. This annual event observed on 29 July, aims to create awareness on tiger conservation.
questions.solution:
Sentence C comes first and introduces the subject of the passage - 'International Tiger Day'. The next sentence to follow should be the one which informs when it is observed. Sentence D mentions the same, hence it follows next.

Sentence B follows and mentions the purpose of observing this day. Sentence A concludes the passage by informing that it is not observed only in India, but in the neighbouring countries of Bangladesh and Nepal as well.

So, the correct order is CDBA.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentence in the right order to form meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. "Excellently well," said she, "we have everything that we want; I have but one prayer, that we may have a heavy storm of rain to water our plants." B. A man who had two daughters married one to a gardener and the other to a potter. C. Off he went to the potter's home and asked his other daughter how matters were with her. D. After a while he paid a visit to the gardener's home and asked his daughter how she was, and how it fared with her.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentence in the right order to form meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. "Excellently well," said she, "we have everything that we want; I have but one prayer, that we may have a heavy storm of rain to water our plants."

B. A man who had two daughters married one to a gardener and the other to a potter.

C. Off he went to the potter's home and asked his other daughter how matters were with her.

D. After a while he paid a visit to the gardener's home and asked his daughter how she was, and how it fared with her.
questions.solution:
Sentence B comes first as it introduces the subjects of the paragraph - a man and his two daughters whom he got married to a gardener and a potter.

Sentences D and A form a pair DA in which sentence D informs that he visited his daughter who was married to a gardener and asked about her well-being. Sentence A mentions the response of his daughter.

Sentence C mentions that then he proceeded towards his other daughter's home, meaning that first he visited the daughter married to a gardener, and then he visited the other daughter. So, DAC will form a triplet.

So, the correct order is BDAC.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.
